messages:
ali: Heads-up - we promoted async-decoder scheduling + kernel-merge (v1) to a 2% canary on prod this morning. Aim: lower tail latency by reducing kernel launch overhead and improving decoder packing. :rocket:
bryce: Replayed 48h of mixed-prod traffic. High-level wins: p50 -15%, p95 -12%, p99 -25%. Token compute cost ~13% lower. Biggest lift on long-sequence streaming + multi-token decode routes.
canary-bot: Canary report uploaded: https://internal.redwood/bench/1897654321
```
shard-mean:
- baseline p50 42ms -> canary p50 35.7ms (-15%)
- baseline p95 220ms -> canary p95 193.6ms (-12%)
- baseline p99 980ms -> canary p99 735ms (-25%)
- cost/1k tokens: $0.095 -> $0.083 (-13%)
- 5xx rate: 0.04% -> 0.045% (no signal)
```
sophia: Nice numbers. Any host/GPU memory regressions or unexpected increase in kernel queue length? Need explicit rollback thresholds for the PD playbook.
victor: Canary config and rollback rules we used: 
```
canary:
  pct: 2
  ramp: 2 -> 20 over 30m -> 100 over 3h
  eval_window: 10m
  rollback_triggers:
    p99_rel_increase_pct: 15
    error_rate_rel_increase_pct: 0.6
    gpu_mem_growth_mb: 80
    kernel_queue_tail_ms: 120
```
bryce: Observed no sustained GPU memory drift. There was a brief kernel-queue stall on shard-9 for ~50s during ramp that auto-fell back to the stable kernel; no customer-visible errors. The kernel-merge improves batching for streaming decodes by merging small kernels into a fused launch which cuts per-call overhead.
ali: Monitoring hooks added: runtime.decoder.async.*, runtime.kernel.merge.*, gpu.memory.delta. PagerDuty on for 90m. If clean, plan to ramp to 20% at +90m and finish roll by EOD.
sophia: Can product get a customer-friendly one-liner + one stat for the weekly? Avoid internal jargon.
ali: Draft for product: "Runtime optimizations reduced typical response times by ~15% and high-percentile latency by ~25% for streaming and multi-token decode flows; estimated token cost savings ~13%."
victor: I'll attach a seq-length vs p99 heatmap and a brief note on the fallback conditions to the canary artifact. Also added a short experiment note about how the fused kernel behaves with mixed-precision quantization.
bryce: One operational note: we keep an automatic pin for requests with >2048 tokens to the stable path until we validate long-run stability. That avoids larger tail risk during the ramp.
ali: Great work everyone. If no regressions by 15:30 UTC we flip the final switch. :tada:
